simple: Git is a tool that saves every version of your code, so you can go back if something breaks.
analogy: Like saving photos of your rangoli after every step — if you smudge it, you can see exactly how it looked before.
example: A developer uses Git to undo a change that broke the login page.

simple: GitHub is a website where people store their Git projects online and share them with others.
analogy: Like a Google Drive for code, where your whole class can see and add to the same notes.
example: Recruiters open your GitHub profile to see the projects you have built.

simple: A repository (repo) is one project folder that Git tracks, with all its files and history.
analogy: Like a single notebook for one subject — all Physics notes go in the Physics notebook.
example: Priya created a repository called 'sales-analysis' for her SQL project.

simple: A commit is one saved snapshot of your changes, with a short message saying what you changed.
analogy: Like an entry in a shop's ledger book: date, what changed, and who did it.
example: "Added monthly sales chart" is a good commit message.

simple: An API is a way for one app to ask another app for data or to do a task.
analogy: Like a waiter in a restaurant: you give the order, the waiter brings it from the kitchen. You never enter the kitchen.
example: A weather app uses an API to get today's temperature in Chennai.

simple: SQL is a language used to ask a database questions and get exact answers.
analogy: Like asking the kirana shop anna: "Give me all Parle-G packets that came this week." He finds exactly that.
example: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city = 'Madurai'; lists all customers from Madurai.

simple: JOIN is an SQL command that combines two tables using a common column.
analogy: Like matching your class attendance register with the marks register using roll numbers.
example: JOIN the orders table with the customers table to see which city each order came from.

simple: GROUP BY is an SQL command that puts rows into groups so you can total or count each group.
analogy: Like sorting a pile of wedding gifts by family and counting how many came from each family.
example: GROUP BY city shows total sales for each city.

simple: A schema is the plan of a database: which tables exist and what columns each one has.
analogy: Like the printed columns in an attendance register — Roll No, Name, Date — before anyone fills it in.
example: The schema says the 'orders' table has order_id, date, and amount.

simple: A database is an organised place to store lots of data so it can be searched quickly.
analogy: Like a well-arranged medical shop where every medicine is in a labelled drawer.
example: Swiggy stores every restaurant and order in a database.

simple: Frontend is the part of a website or app that you see and click.
analogy: Like the front of a restaurant — tables, menu and decoration that customers see.
example: The buttons and colours on the Zomato app are the frontend.

simple: Backend is the hidden part of an app that stores data and does the work behind the screen.
analogy: Like the restaurant kitchen — customers never see it, but all the cooking happens there.
example: When you pay on an app, the backend checks your payment and saves the order.

simple: CI/CD automatically tests new code and puts it live, so updates are fast and safe.
analogy: Like a factory conveyor belt that checks every packet of biscuits and sends good ones straight to shops.
example: Every time a developer saves code, CI/CD runs tests and updates the website.

simple: Docker packs an app with everything it needs so it runs the same on any computer.
analogy: Like a tiffin box that holds the full meal — rice, sambar, curd — so it tastes the same wherever you open it.
example: A team uses Docker so the app works the same on a laptop and on the server.

simple: The cloud means using computers and storage owned by big companies over the internet, instead of your own.
analogy: Like taking an auto-rickshaw instead of buying a car — you pay only when you use it.
example: Startups rent servers on AWS cloud instead of buying machines.

simple: OCR is technology that reads text from a photo or scanned page and turns it into typed text.
analogy: Like a friend who reads your handwritten notes aloud and types them into WhatsApp.
example: Banking apps use OCR to read your PAN card number from a photo.

simple: A framework is a ready-made structure for building apps, so you don't start from zero.
analogy: Like the bamboo frame of a pandal — you just add the cloth and decorations.
example: React and Next.js are frameworks for building websites.

simple: A library is a collection of ready-made code you can use in your own program.
analogy: Like buying ready-made masala powder instead of grinding every spice yourself.
example: Pandas is a Python library for working with tables of data.

simple: A dataset is a collection of related data, usually in a table with rows and columns.
analogy: Like a class marks sheet — each row is a student, each column is a subject.
example: A dataset of 10,000 Flipkart orders with date, product and price.

simple: A dashboard is one screen of charts and numbers that shows how things are going at a glance.
analogy: Like a bike's speedometer panel — speed, fuel and distance all in one place.
example: A sales manager checks a dashboard every morning to see yesterday's sales.

simple: Regression is a maths method to find how one thing changes when another changes, and to predict it.
analogy: Like guessing a mango's price from its size after seeing many mangoes at the market.
example: Using regression to predict house rent in Bengaluru from its size and area.

simple: Python is a popular, beginner-friendly programming language used for data, websites and AI.
analogy: Like English among languages — easy to start with and used almost everywhere.
example: Data analysts use Python to clean data and make charts.

simple: Pandas is a Python library for reading, cleaning and analysing tables of data.
analogy: Like a super-powered Excel you control by typing instructions.
example: df.groupby('city').sum() in Pandas totals sales for each city.

simple: A pivot table in Excel quickly summarises a big table, like totals per month or per product.
analogy: Like a shopkeeper turning a long bill book into a short list: total sold of each item.
example: A pivot table shows total sales per region in two clicks.

simple: Power BI is a Microsoft tool for making interactive dashboards and reports from data.
analogy: Like a scoreboard at a cricket match that updates live and shows all the key numbers.
example: A company uses Power BI to show monthly revenue to its managers.

simple: Tableau is a tool for turning data into charts and dashboards by dragging and dropping.
analogy: Like decorating a cake with a piping bag — you shape the data into a nice picture easily.
example: An analyst builds a Tableau map showing sales in each Indian state.

simple: Statistics is the maths of collecting and understanding numbers — averages, spread and patterns.
analogy: Like a cricket commentator saying a batsman averages 45 runs — one number that sums up many matches.
example: Finding the average order value and how much it varies each month.

simple: Visualization means showing data as charts or pictures so it's easy to understand.
analogy: Like a train route map — much easier to follow than a list of station names.
example: A bar chart comparing sales across 5 cities.

simple: Excel is a spreadsheet app for storing numbers in rows and columns and doing calculations.
analogy: Like a smart notebook with a calculator built into every box.
example: Using SUM and VLOOKUP in Excel to prepare a monthly expense report.

simple: Data cleaning means fixing messy data — removing duplicates, filling blanks, correcting mistakes.
analogy: Like picking stones out of rice before cooking.
example: Changing 'chennai', 'Chenai' and 'CHENNAI' all into 'Chennai'.

simple: A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is an important number that shows if a business is doing well.
analogy: Like your CGPA — one number that shows how your semester went.
example: Monthly revenue growth is a KPI for a sales team.

simple: Machine learning is teaching computers to learn patterns from data instead of giving them fixed rules.
analogy: Like a child learning to spot ripe mangoes after seeing many, not from a rulebook.
example: YouTube uses machine learning to suggest videos you might like.

simple: An algorithm is a clear list of steps to solve a problem.
analogy: Like a recipe for making dosa — follow the steps in order and you get the result.
example: Google Maps uses an algorithm to find the fastest route.

simple: JavaScript is the programming language that makes websites interactive.
analogy: Like the electricity in a house — HTML is the walls, JavaScript makes the fans and lights work.
example: JavaScript shows a pop-up when you click 'Add to cart'.

simple: HTML is the language that gives a web page its structure — headings, paragraphs, images, buttons.
analogy: Like the walls and rooms of a house before painting.
example:
Welcome

makes a big heading on a page.

simple: CSS is the language that styles a web page — colours, fonts, spacing and layout.
analogy: Like the paint, curtains and furniture that make a house look nice.
example: CSS makes a button indigo with rounded corners.

simple: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces from reusable pieces called components.
analogy: Like LEGO blocks — build small pieces once and reuse them to build big things.
example: Instagram's website is built with React.

simple: Linux is a free operating system that runs most of the world's servers.
analogy: Like the Indian Railways network — you rarely see it, but it quietly carries most of the load.
example: Websites like Wikipedia run on Linux servers.

simple: Kubernetes manages many Docker containers, starting, stopping and scaling them automatically.
analogy: Like a railway station master who decides which train goes on which platform and adds coaches when it's crowded.
example: During a big sale, Kubernetes adds more copies of the app to handle the crowd.

simple: A server is a computer that runs all the time to give data or websites to other computers.
analogy: Like a 24-hour ATM that gives cash to anyone who asks correctly.
example: When you open Google, a server sends you the search page.

simple: A query is a question you ask a database, usually written in SQL.
analogy: Like asking a librarian: "Show me all books by R.K. Narayan."
example: A query to find the top 5 products by sales last month.

simple: A CSV is a simple file that stores a table as text, with commas between the values.
analogy: Like writing a shopping list as 'item, quantity, price' on each line.
example: You can download your bank statement as a CSV and open it in Excel.
